name: comp-265

frames.best_why: Range is narrowed to $200-$533 so both handles, the filled band, the histogram and the item count are all readable.

tagline: A histogram of prices with a two-handle filter drawn straight across it.
summary: A price filter that stacks a row of thin histogram bars above a dual-handle slider. Below sit min and max price fields, and an outlined button reports how many items fall in the range.
appearance: A small Price slider label tops a band of many narrow grey bars of uneven height. A two-handle track lies across their base, with a solid white band between the handles. Two outlined fields labelled Min price and Max price follow, then a full-width outlined button.
behaviour: Dragging either handle reshapes the white band and rewrites both price fields and the number on the button. Typing in a field moves the matching handle and recalculates the count.
demo_content: A fixed list of 120 item prices from 80 to 900; the fields open at $200 and $780 and the button reads Show 93 items.
search_phrases: filter a list by minimum and maximum cost
distribution chart behind a range bar
two handles over a bar chart
narrow results with lower and upper limits
price filter with boxes for each bound
data distribution slider for a catalogue
range picker showing how many match
use_when: Shoppers should see where the stock is concentrated while setting a budget window.
avoid_when: The chart is built from a hardcoded price list, so real catalogue data has to be wired in.
customise: The price list, label and currency symbol sit in the source; bucket count and formatting need edits, and the count button follows the data.
weight_why: Forty bars and two inputs; counts are recomputed only when the range moves.

a11y.note: Fields and slider are labelled, but the changing item count is plain button text and is not announced.

issues: Bars keep the same grey inside and outside the range, so the selection highlight does not show.
polish_why: Well built composition of chart, slider and fields; the missing bar highlight is the one flaw.
